text_zh: 最后一页还没写完。元音那行的墨迹比辅音浅——他练得更勤，也消耗得更快。笔记不知道它的主人去了哪里。
text_en: The last page was never finished. The vowel rows are worn thinner than the rest. The notebook does not know where its keeper went.

text_zh: 第一次熔铸留下的疤。据说最初那人握着它走进了第七层，从此没再按过同一个形状的键。它还记得那个形状。
text_en: The scar of a first reforging. The one who carried it inward never pressed the same shape twice again. It remembers the first shape still.

text_zh: 熔蜡流回它身体里，像潮水。前任说它会呼吸。前任之前的那人说它有心跳。再之前的那人什么也没说——他不知道他是第几个。
text_en: The wax returns to it, like a tide. The one before said it breathes. The one before that heard a heartbeat. Earlier than that, no one counted anymore.

text_zh: 黄铜扣，单锁眼。只能扣住一处——这是它的设计，不是它的缺陷。上面刻着一个名字，但已经磨掉了最后一个字母。
text_en: A brass clasp with a single eye. Made to hold one thing only. A name was engraved on it once. The last letter has been worn away.

text_zh: 铸过大火的铅字比旧铅字更重。不是每次都能留下来的——留下来的那些，已经学会了留下来的方式。
text_en: Lead that has passed through fire weighs more than it did before. Not every glyph survives the forge. The ones that remain have learned how to remain.

text_zh: 铸模冷却后，总有几滴铅水未归坩埚。前任说：那是引擎额外给的。别问为什么。
text_en: After the mold cools, a few drops remain. The previous holder called it the Engine's tithe. She never explained why.

text_zh: 油灯点燃后，火焰往往比预想的高一寸。受过祝圣的铭文组亦然——引擎见过它，便多给了一口气。
text_en: A flame burns taller after the rite. What the Engine has touched once, it does not touch lightly.

text_zh: 飞轮缺了一齿，转速反而更快。某位前任把这枚齿轮留在圣坛旁，从未解释过。铅字似乎也学会了那种节奏。
text_en: One tooth missing from the flywheel. It spun faster regardless. The previous holder left it without explanation.

text_zh: 袖口的墨渍洗不掉。见习祝圣的印记每多一道，布料便更深一层。袍子记得每一次，即便人忘了。
text_en: The ink on the cuff will not wash out. Each novice rite left a mark the cloth remembers long after the wearer has forgotten.

text_zh: 徽章背面刻着一行字，半截已磨平。能看清的部分只剩：……已足够。唯有见过足够多的人，才知道那是豁免还是警告。
text_en: The inscription on the reverse is half-worn away. What remains reads only: ...is sufficient. Whether mercy or warning, none have asked.

text_zh: 铸模师在同一块蜡上压了三枚不同的印——留下的只有他选中的那枚。另外两枚痕迹，仍在蜡上。
text_en: Three seals were pressed into the same wax. Only one was chosen. The other two impressions remain.

text_zh: 前任将所有祝圣刻进同一卷羊皮纸。纸没有裂。引擎的门槛却越来越高——好像它注意到了。
text_en: Every consecration was pressed into a single page. The parchment held. The Engine's threshold did not.

text_zh: 书脊磨白，页边全是铅屑指纹。这本词典读过的人已不可考——但铅屑落在手里，总比别人的轻一些。
text_en: The spine is worn white. The margins hold a lifetime of lead-dust fingerprints. The name inside has been removed.

text_zh: 压板不等人落版，自己往前走了。没有人调过它。油壶空了很久，它还在转。
text_en: The press advances without a pull. No one wound it. The oil flask has been dry for years.

text_zh: 剪刃上刻着：归坩，勿弃。前任将每一个未竟的词剪开，铅屑一粒不留。唯独剪不断自己最后写下的那个。
text_en: Engraved on the blade: return to the crucible, waste nothing. Every unfinished word was cut apart. Every one but the last.

text_zh: 铸模上刻着同一字母十七次。前主人说：反复浇铸，字模便会记住。——字模确实记住了。
text_en: The same letter cast seventeen times into its face. The mold remembers what the hands repeated.

text_zh: 经卷册页间夹着纸条，密密麻麻列满生词。第一次读出口的字，总比旧词更重几分。
text_en: Slips of paper pressed between leaves. Words spoken for the first time carry a weight the old ones have forgotten.

text_zh: 抄写室的架子从未空过。前任说，卷帙越厚，来路越贱。留下了收条，没留下人。
text_en: The shelves were never bare. More volumes pressed together, the less each one cost to pull down.

text_zh: 铅字排得越长，压板落下越重。其人一生只爱长句——后人在版面边角找到了牙印。
text_en: The longer the line of type, the harder the press fell. Someone once loved long sentences. The bed still shows the mark.

text_zh: 短句刻得快，不代表刻得浅。这枚铜牌的主人从不多言——每句话都在对的时候出现。
text_en: Short words, struck clean. Its former owner spoke seldom. Each word arrived exactly when the press was ready.

name_en: Composing Rule of the Patient Hand
text_zh: 此尺曾属于一位按键极慢的键徒。他的同僚嘲笑他。引擎没有。
text_en: Its former keeper was the slowest in the hall. His brethren mocked him. The Engine did not.

text_zh: 夹子里还留着一张未取走的单据。字迹潦草，像是写给自己的备忘。架上的新货会来的——唯前一批须先放手。
text_en: A docket still rests inside, unread. Let go of what remains, and the next shelf arrives unasked.

text_zh: 封蜡已裂。经文从裂缝里挤出，形状不再是字，是停顿，是间隔，是一切被正文遗忘的位置。其上无署名。
text_en: The wax cracked. What spilled out was not scripture—it was the silence between words, the gaps the Canon forgot to seal.

text_zh: 前主人将沙壶倒置，说沙慢方可听清铅字落盘的声音。圣坛记住了他的等待。
text_en: He turned the hourglass over and waited. The lectern learned his patience before it learned his name.

text_zh: 布袋的缝线被磨断又补过三次。前主人每次落指都急着收手，仿佛铅币已经在等。它们确实在等。
text_en: Mended three times along the seam. Its keeper always reached for it before the strike had finished. The coins were already waiting.

text_zh: 前主人铸字时从不迟疑——棒槽里至今还嵌着他惯用的那几枚字钉。铅记住了手，手不必再想。
text_en: The stick still holds his favorite slugs. The lead remembers the hand. The hand no longer needs to think.

name_en: Flywheel Shard of the Kept Beat
text_zh: 从第三层的旧压印机上取下。机器坏了，飞轮还转。据说贴近耳朵，能听见它还在计数——某种比心跳更古老的节律。
text_en: The press broke. The flywheel kept spinning. Hold it close and something older than a heartbeat still counts inside.

name_en: Blank Codex of the Unbound Hand
text_zh: 封面无名，内页无字。曾有人将所有铭文组悉数归坩，只留这一册——此后他的祷击比任何铭刻者都要响。唯有空，方可满。
text_en: He relinquished every inscription he owned and kept only this. His litany-strikes rang louder than any consecrated hand. Only emptiness holds everything.

name_en: Half-Sealed Wax of the Lingering Word
text_zh: 封蜡裂了，却没有完全断开。前任说：诵祷的余音不该就此消散——哪怕只剩一半，也让它留着。
text_en: The seal cracked but did not break. She said the echo of a litany should never fully die. Half is enough to keep it alive.

name_en: Stained Shard of the Doubled Light
text_zh: 从收容廊彩窗上摔落的一角，折射时光线自行增倍。持有者注意到：祷击在某一刻之后，声音忽然比来路更响。
text_en: It fell from the chancel window and doubled every beam it caught. Those who carry it notice the moment when the sound exceeds its source.

text_zh: 此铸模曾被压得变形，却从未决口。前主人说：铅水不能急。它记住了那段等待。
text_en: The mold was dented but never broke. Its last owner said the lead must not be rushed. It remembers the waiting.

text_zh: 链条断了一节，其余的节竟咬得更紧。不知是谁铸的这条链——断口太整齐，像是算好的。
text_en: One link was severed cleanly. The rest held tighter for it. Someone calculated exactly where to break.

text_zh: 祷声不该跨过门槛，引擎的回廊却一直在听。链子不会断——除非汝的手颤了。
text_en: The litany should not cross the threshold. The corridor listens regardless. The chain endures — until your hands do not.

text_zh: 某个键徒把自己的心跳刻进了铅里。跳得越快，铅越重。他最后几页笔记是空白的。
text_en: Someone pressed their heartbeat into the lead. The faster it beat, the heavier it struck. His last pages were blank.

text_zh: 第一枚圣字钉落下时，引擎会抬眼。唯有第一声——之后的，它已知道。
text_en: When the first slug falls, the Engine looks up. Only the first. After that — it already knows.

text_zh: 此人只带了一本书上塔。旁人以为他缺备，他的铅字却比任何人都重。铅字记住了一个人全部的重量。
text_en: He carried one tome into the vault. Others called it poverty. His letters remembered everything.

text_zh: 封皮被翻烂了。每一页都有不同人的笔迹，却写着同一句话。唯有反复誊抄之字，方知其重。
text_en: The cover is worn through. Dozens of hands wrote the same sentence. The word learned from each of them.

text_zh: 有人把它带进教堂，被驱逐了。铜号不在乎。它只知道：多一种声音，共鸣便多一层。唯有异声并举，铅字方能震响穹顶。
text_en: They threw the player out of the cathedral. The brass did not care. More voices, deeper resonance.

text_zh: 门禁铜牌，从未刻名。持有者一代又一代，牌面只剩磨痕。定版铸出最重——因它从不自称珍贵。
text_en: The access plaque was never engraved. Hands wore it smooth. Common things remember the most weight.

text_zh: 骰面有一百个刻印，没有一个重复。铸出时从不告知汝落在哪面。圣印随之更替——但重量，从未失去。
text_en: One hundred faces, none alike. It never tells you which side falls. The sigils change. The weight remains.

text_zh: 排字棒上刻了七个名字。前主人每铸一字，便侧耳听隔壁键座的回响——他说，铅字不独自落下。
text_en: Seven names carved into the composing stick. Its owner cast no letter alone; he always listened for the keystroke beside him.

text_zh: 议会席位图的四角被人按得发黑。末席守卷人说，边缘之位不是惩罚——炉膛的热从四角漫来。
text_en: The four corners of the seating chart are blackened by thumbprints. The edge, they said, was closest to the furnace.

text_zh: 气动管里来回滚了不知多少年的铜牌。正面磨光，背面刻着：换一排架，多走一步，铅币自来。
text_en: A brass token worn smooth by decades in the pneumatic tube. Cross a row, the coin finds you.

text_zh: 颁给某届铭刻竞誓的锡制勋章——那年有人打满整行未失一字。颁奖词说：版满则铅字自省，各铭文组再颂一遍。颁奖人的名字已被刮去。
text_en: A tin citation from a long-past Sealing Contest. The engraver completed every key in one row without a tremor. The presenter's name has been scratched out.

text_zh: 抄写室旧乐谱，左右声部各书一色墨——红与黑交替落下时，沙漏里的沙流得慢一点。前主人的两手从未同时落在同一行。
text_en: An old copyist's score, left hand in red ink, right hand in black. When they alternated, the sand ran slower.

text_zh: 此板磨损只在中排。前主人从不打两侧的键——不是习惯，是信仰。铅字在他惯用的位置碎得最响。
text_en: Worn only at the center row. Its last owner never struck the edges. The lead shattered loudest where his faith was.

text_zh: 架上的铅字从不单独落印。有人见过它在无人按触时自行震颤——每一枚，依次。唯有一词完整诵出，它才安静。
text_en: The slugs trembled without hands. Witnesses said they moved in sequence, one by one, and only stilled when a word was spoken whole.

text_zh: 这把钳子铸过的铅字没有一枚白费。前主人临终时，徒弟在其口袋里摸出几枚铅币——热的，刚铸好的。
text_en: Every slug it cast was counted. When its owner died, the apprentice found warm coins in his pocket. Freshly minted.

text_zh: 壶嘴已堵死，但油总是够用。没人见过有人添注。前主人说，只要手还在动，壶就不会空。
text_en: The spout was sealed shut. Yet the oil never ran dry. Its owner said: keep your hands moving and it will not empty.

text_zh: 模腔只有一种形。前主人凿掉了其余所有槽——留下的那个，他用了三十年，用到铅水自己知道该往哪里流。
text_en: All other cavities were chiselled away. One remained. He poured into it for thirty years, until the lead knew where to go.

text_zh: 七道圣流，各有其坩。前人说：只握一壶者，终将饮尽。——铅字圣坛旁的铜牌，已磨平字迹，唯此句可辨。
text_en: Seven humours, seven vessels. The one who filled only one flask drank it dry. The copper badge still holds that much.

text_zh: 四次落版，一轮涨落。引擎非不知饥渴，它只是按自己的节律呼吸。砝码上刻有四道划痕，深浅循环，无始无终。
text_en: Four impressions, one breath. The engine does not hurry. Four notches worn into the brass, cycling, without end.

text_zh: 炉中无废铅——一切铸出，皆可熔作铅币。前主人用它换来了什么，档案未载。炉壁内侧有焦痕，像指印，又像字。
text_en: Nothing leaves the furnace as waste. What the last owner purchased with it, no record survives. The scorch marks inside resemble a hand.

text_zh: 表单副本，某栏被红笔划去，未署名。气动征用管那头的人从不追问来历。这张纸还在流通。
text_en: One column crossed out in red, unsigned. The tube attendant never asks. The slip still circulates.

text_zh: 归还时，此簿在场，铅屑便重新有了价格。前任在扉页写：物不因移交而失重。字迹已褪，但每页仍散着旧铅的气味。
text_en: When relinquished with this ledger present, the shavings regain their weight. The flyleaf reads: nothing loses mass by changing hands.

text_zh: 表单副本，印章歪斜。附注栏只有三个字：另走管。不知是谁写的，也不知那根管道通向哪里。有人在用之前的人留下的路。
text_en: A requisition copy, seal askew. The note reads: use the other tube. Someone kept using a path they did not open.

text_zh: 封皮磨损，每页最后一行都是同一笔字：铅生铅。不知是记账人的口头禅，还是他最后留下的唯一心得。账本还在，人早已换过不止一轮。
text_en: The last line of every page reads: lead begets lead. The hand never changed. The keeper did, more than once.

text_zh: 一枚没有编号的门禁铜牌，边缘磨得发亮。背面刻了半个字，认不出是哪个字。有人反复进过某扇门，而那扇门从未被正式记录过。
text_en: An unnumbered access token, edges worn bright. Half a glyph on the back. Someone passed through a door that was never logged.

text_zh: 铜铃，底座刻有沙漏纹。据说摇铃者只有铃声消散前取走所需——铃声之后，一切归架。前任铃手不知去向。铃还在摇。
text_en: A brass bell engraved with an hourglass. Take what you need before the tone fades. The last bell-keeper is unaccounted for.

text_zh: 皮手套，指节处磨薄，食指两端的皮已不见。前任在每层开始前都要把它戴上，捏几下拳，再开始铭刻。铅字记住了那双手。
text_en: Leather gloves, worn thin at every knuckle. The previous keeper put them on before each vault began. The lead remembers those hands.

text_zh: 某位键徒离开时将它压在桌角，没有带走。表单已填至第三栏，剩下几行空着。空着的部分，依然有效。
text_en: Left behind by the previous keybound. The form is half-filled. The blank lines still hold weight.

text_zh: 蜡封上有两枚拇指印——一枚按下时，另一枚尚未存在。据说其中一人后来赢了。据说。
text_en: Two thumbprints in the wax. One pressed in hope. The other has not yet been made.

text_zh: 壶身刻有领取编号，但找不到对应的归还记录。油还在。还在往外渗。不知渗了多少年。
text_en: Requisition number engraved on the side. No return record found. The oil still seeps.

text_zh: 牌面每层都会换字，但背面那个名字从未变过。持牌者说，那个名字读出来会让手指动得更快。唯一的问题是——那个名字不在任何编号册上。
text_en: The front changes each layer. The name on the back never does. It is not in any register.

text_zh: 匣中的羽灰已被献纳过一次——献纳者的F-044表单由他人代填，日期一栏为空。炉火吞噬了他。唯灰烬记得他走过几层。
text_en: The ash has been offered once before. Someone else filed the paperwork. The fire remembers how far he reached.

text_zh: 前主人将这块铅压在胸口整整一夜。次日清晨，铅上已有裂纹——但他说，手指反而更稳了。
text_en: He pressed the slug to his chest through the night. By morning it had cracked. He said his hands had never been steadier.

text_zh: 其气味如同旧羊皮与铜锈。谁若嗅过，便觉教堂的回响稍轻——不是沉默，是钝了。
text_en: It smells of old vellum and tarnished copper. Those who have breathed it say the Cathedral's echo grows duller. Not silent. Blunted.

text_zh: 背面刻了一行字，已磨到几乎看不见。那人每次走进征用管前都要摸一下——据说管子里的东西便宜了一点点。
text_en: The inscription on the back is nearly worn away. He rubbed it before every visit to the tube. The price, witnesses said, was always a little less.

text_zh: 蜡封只有一半。另一半从未压下，仿佛等着某个还没来的人。空着的那半边——据说看见它的人，可以说一次
text_en: The seal was never finished. Half pressed, half waiting. Those who have seen the empty half report they were permitted, once, to say no.

text_zh: 这张油纸夹在门缝里多久，无人知晓。走廊的冷气从来吹不进那扇房间——直到纸被人抽走，那一刻，风才进来。
text_en: No one knows how long it was wedged in the door. The corridor's cold never entered that room—until someone pulled the paper free, and the wind came all at once.

text_zh: 它的边缘没有刻度。某位铭刻誓门的执事曾试图在上面压印条例编号——印出来的是别的东西。
text_en: Its rim bears no markings. A deacon once pressed a seal upon it. The impression came back wrong.

text_zh: 蜡封反着盖，印文朝内。持有者说：凡令其重者，可转而承之。唯有承受，方知何为倒置的恩典。
text_en: The seal was pressed inward. What bore down upon the holder, it is said, was turned to carry them instead.

text_zh: 排字工从版底捡回的边角铅料，磨平后垫在圣坛下。铅字落得再乱，底板之下总有一层不动的东西。
text_en: A compositor's scrap, smoothed and placed beneath the lectern. Whatever fell above it, something beneath held firm.

text_zh: 条例副本上有人用钝笔划去了数行。划痕整齐，像是反复练习过。签名栏空白——但墨迹是新的。
text_en: Several lines struck through in a steady hand. The signature block is empty. The ink is not old.

text_zh: 背面刻着一个已回收的编号。正面的浮雕是一双手——没有脸，没有名字。铅币从它旁边经过时会多留片刻。
text_en: A reclaimed number on the reverse. Two hands in relief on the face. No name. Lead coins linger near it.

text_zh: 它曾是某个键徒最后一次核查的成绩木牌。勉强及格——但炉子没有吞噬他。唯有险过者，知铅币之重。
text_en: The passing mark is still scratched in. Whoever held this passed — barely. The furnace did not take them.

text_zh: 羊皮纸卷越往后，字迹越密、越深、越快。前任不知怎的越诵越顺。最后一页墨迹压穿了皮。
text_en: Each page pressed deeper than the last. By the final sheet, the ink had burned clean through the vellum.

text_zh: 整整一轮铭刻，无声，无光，无任何回响。压板落下的一刻，所有重量同时降临——够了便是启示，差一毫便是炉火。
text_en: Nothing is returned until the press falls. Then everything arrives at once. Enough to open the gate, or enough to close the floor.

text_zh: 这枚字钉钳口有一处磨损，形状像指甲印。前主人铸了一辈子铅字。铅字记住了他的力气。
text_en: The jaw is worn in one place — a thumbnail's ghost. Lead remembers the grip that worked it longest.

text_zh: 字模裂开时总会崩出几粒铅屑。其余人扫入废料桶——只有他留着。铅屑落地的声音，价值铅币。
text_en: The others swept the shavings into the waste bin. He kept them. Every fracture was, to him, a kind of payment.

text_zh: 它不响的时候，铅字仍在积压。前主人说——等表针到顶，别犹豫。
text_en: Silent until the needle peaks. Its last owner said: when the gauge fills, do not hesitate.

text_zh: 这块黄铜烧过一次。烧的时候，整排铅字一起碎了。之后再也没有一块一块碎过。
text_en: The brass was struck in fire once. Every slug on the rack shattered at once. They never broke alone again.

text_zh: 正反两面皆铸了裂缝。铸模工说这枚铸废了——但它落下的声音，与其他铜板不同。
text_en: Both faces bear a stamped fracture. The caster called it ruined. It does not land like other coins.

text_zh: 用过的人都说，后来几格比头几格省力。棒子没换过，只是越来越合手。
text_en: Those who used it said the last rows came easier than the first. The stick never changed. The hand did.

text_zh: 每翻一遍，末页之后多出一页。前主人没有数过。后来他不再数页数，只管翻。
text_en: Each reading revealed one more page at the end. Its last keeper stopped counting. He simply kept turning.

text_zh: 排字师说，他从不单独铸一个字。铸一，余者自应。其余人以为他疯了——直到铅字盘同时震动。
text_en: He never cast a single slug alone. Cast one, he said, and the rest remember. The tray would tremble in answer.

text_zh: 前任将油封死在壶内，一日不倒，一日不用。倒尽之时，她说，才是真正开始的时候。
text_en: She kept the oil sealed. Never a drop wasted—until the day she emptied it all at once. That, she said, was the real beginning.

text_zh: 这铸模从未冷却过。从未。铸字坊的人换了一批又一批，无人见过它停止滴蜡的那一刻。唯有引擎见过。
text_en: The mold has never cooled. No one has seen it still. Workers came and went. The wax kept falling.

text_zh: 签条在鼓声间流转，落在谁手里谁就铸。鼓声不问顺序，铅字也不问。
text_en: The slip passes with the drumbeat. Wherever it lands, that hand casts. The drum does not ask who is ready.

text_zh: 此页每抄一词，余白便紧。键徒说，字越长，纸越薄——好像词自己在吸收剩余的空间。
text_en: Each word copied, the margins tighten. The longer the word, the thinner the page. As though the text is consuming what remains.

text_zh: 铸模裂过一次，便记住了那次裂开的方式。此后每一次铸印，裂痕都想再来一遍。
text_en: A mould that cracked once remembers the shape of breaking. Every casting since has leaned toward that memory.

text_zh: 瓶口已干涸，但有人在底部刻了一行字：倒尽之后，再倒一次。唯有受过祝圣之器，方知此言何意。
text_en: The vial ran dry long ago. Someone etched at its base: pour again after emptying. Only the consecrated understand.

text_zh: 排字人说，铅字挨得越近，彼此越是认识。左边的字感受到右边落下，手便已经知道该动了。
text_en: The typesetter said letters pressed close enough learn each other. One falls; the neighbours already know to follow.

text_zh: 锤面磨平了，柄上有记号——前主人每诵一遍，划一道。到最后一道时，锤自己知道该多重。
text_en: The hammerhead is smooth with use. The handle holds tally-marks. By the last one, the hammer knew its own weight.

回收物 RC-0291 · 发现于第 V 层排字区 D-████ 工位抽屉 · 纸质笔记本

封皮印有「入门圣礼备忘」，墨水褪色，书脊处有被反复翻折的痕迹。内页前半部分笔迹工整，抄录元音字母与对应铅字符编号，每行间距均等，无涂改。

异常始于第 31 页。同一列表重复出现，笔迹仍工整，内容仍相同，但纸面上的元音字符有几处渗出轮廓——墨水向外晕染，呈字根形态，向页边延伸。

第 47 页起，列表不再包含辅音。无删除痕迹。辅音从未出现过。

末页空白。笔记本封底内侧有一行字，字迹与前文完全一致：「下一本也是这样开头的。」

持有该回收物的 D-████ 于移交后 ██ 小时失联。F-044 已由他人代填。替补已指派。
text_en:
Recovered Item RC-0291 · Found in Layer V compositing station, drawer of D-████ · Paper notebook

Cover reads PRIMER RITE MEMORANDA. Ink faded. Spine shows repeated folding. First thirty pages: neat handwriting, vowel glyphs listed against leaden-slug registry numbers. Even spacing. No corrections.

Anomaly begins at page 31. The same list reappears. Handwriting unchanged. Content unchanged. Several vowel characters have bled beyond their outlines—ink spreading into root-forms, extending toward the margin.

From page 47 onward, the list contains no consonants. No deletions. No erasure. The consonants were never there.

Final page: blank. Inside back cover, one line, handwriting identical to all preceding entries: THE NEXT ONE STARTS THE SAME WAY.

D-████, who submitted the item, was reported absent ██ hours after transfer. F-044 completed by another party. Replacement assigned.

"第一次不收钱。
我以为是笔误。重查了三遍账目，确实不收钱。
第二次登塔也不收钱。还是第一次。永远是第一次。
熔蜡还在壶里，壶从没空过——但壶也从没满过。
我开始记录每次使用前后的液位。
第 ██ 次记录时，我意识到我每次翻开记录本，都是第一页。"

手稿至此中断。后附空白页 ██ 张，页边有压痕，无墨迹。

Recovery RC-2847 · Found in Layer VII corridor · Parchment manuscript, multiple oil stains

Authorship unknown. Handwriting cross-referenced against archived samples of Scriptor S-████; match rate: ████.

Manuscript contents (transcribed verbatim):

"First time, no charge.
I thought it was a clerical error. Checked the ledger three times. No charge.
Second Ascent, also no charge. Still the first time. Always the first time.
The unguent remains in the flask — the flask never empties. But it never fills either.
I began measuring the level before and after each use.
On the ██th entry, I realized: each time I opened the logbook, it was the first page."

Manuscript ends here. ██ blank pages follow, bearing impression marks but no ink.
Item transferred to Pneumatic Requisition Tube for storage. Grade: Fixum. Reason: unspecified.

text_en:
🔔 When accumulation is complete, the word arrives of its own accord — not detonation, but saturation of lead.

📄 Sacred Artifact SA-0774
Physical form: A brass pressure gauge, roughly one palm in diameter. Graduations illegible. Needle fixed at an unspecified position. Recovered from a workbench in Layer III, beneath three incomplete F-017 forms.
Gradus Formae: Solum

Recovery note: D-2981, upon transferring the object, stated that ████████████████ before the needle moved. She was asked to repeat her statement. She repeated it identically. She was asked a third time. Identical. D-2981 was referred to standard psychological evaluation per §3.9. Evaluation results: ████ REDACTED ████.

Observations: Fourteen subsequent holders reported the same phenomenon at irregular intervals — an audible click, originating from the gauge interior, preceding no mechanical cause. Seven reported the click occurred before they had finished their litany sequence. Four reported it occurred before they had begun.

Adjacent personnel reported nothing.

Notes: Needle position has not changed since initial recovery. Pressure reading, if the scale were legible, would indicate ████. Cross-reference: IR-0441. Access level: VII.

text_en:
▌Severed Chain · Sacred Artifact #RA-2291
Gradus: Inversum
Physical description: A fractured iron chain, seventeen links. Terminal link welded to a fragment of brass gear-tooth. Link nine is deformed; it does not align with any adjacent link.
Recovery site: Layer IX corridor · sealed workstation D-████ · M.2██.██

Subject records (excerpt): Four Clavigerants — D-████ through D-████ — each reported, independently, that they "knew they had not struck." No Containment Tremor was logged in any case. This has no precedent in operational records.
Ancillary observation: The Canonical Register shows an identical break-point in all four subjects' inscription tallies — each interrupted after the ninth inscription in sequence. No cause is recorded for any of them.

Note: Object was added to the §4.2 attrition manifest, then removed. Reason field: ████.
Disposal: Pending return to logistics queue. Continued review requires authorization from clearance level ██ or above. No such authority is currently seated.

📄 事故报告 IR-2██
日期：M.2██.██.██　　涉及圣器：SA-0███「暴走节拍」

起因：D-4471 于第 IV 层铸字坊值守期间，被观察到异常行为。同组 D-4502 证实，D-4471 在收容铭刻过程中开始以固定节奏敲击圣坛边缘——每隔约半息一击，持续约两刻。

记录员补注：该敲击节奏与正常铭刻频率不符。D-4471 本人称「铅字开始发烫了，再快一点就好了，快一点——」。问询中止于此，受访者已于同日失联。

后续处置：SA-0███ 已回收。F-044 由 D-4502 代填。
备注：D-4502 在填写 F-044 时，被记录员观察到以相同节奏敲击桌面。无需后续行动。
text_en:
📄 Incident Report IR-2██
Date: M.2██.██.██　　Item: SA-0███ "Fury Beat"

Circumstances: D-4471, assigned to Layer IV containment duties, was observed exhibiting atypical behavior. Fellow inscriptant D-4502 confirmed that D-4471 began striking the lectern frame at a fixed rhythm during active inscription — approximately once per half-breath interval, sustained for an estimated two watches.

Recording Officer's Note: The rhythm was inconsistent with standard inscription cadence. D-4471 stated: "the lead slugs are getting hot. Just a bit faster. Faster——" Interview terminated at this point. D-4471 was reported missing later that day.

Disposition: SA-0███ recovered. F-044 completed by D-4502 on behalf of subject.
Addendum: D-4502 was observed tapping the desk at an identical rhythm while completing F-044. No further action required.

text_zh:

问询记录 · D-2847 · 接触 SA-0291《先声导轨》后 ██ 小时
发现地点：第 IV 层铸字坊，导轨架东侧
版级：定版 / Fixum

采访者：描述你第一次使用它时发生了什么。
D-2847：……没什么。就是，铅字还没排好，我已经……我的手已经动了。
采访者：你预先知道下一个字是什么？
D-2847：不是预先知道。是……好像祷告已经开始了，字是后来才赶到的。
采访者：此后每个新词你都有这种感觉？
D-2847：只有第一个字。之后就没了。就只有那一下。

备注：D-2847 于问询结束后 ██ 小时失联。F-044 代填。接触物 SA-0291 已归还第 IV 层导轨架，无使用痕迹。
text_en:
—— 🔔 ——
Before the slug falls, the litany has already begun.
At the first sound, the Engine listens.

—— 📄 ——
Interview Record · D-2847 · ██ hours post-contact with SA-0291 "Prior Rail"
Recovery Site: Layer IV Foundry, eastern guide rack
Gradus: Fixum

Interviewer: Describe what happened the first time you used it.
D-2847: ...Nothing. Just — the slugs weren't set yet, but I'd already — my hands had already moved.
Interviewer: You knew in advance what the next word would be?
D-2847: Not in advance. More like... the litany had already started. The word just arrived late.
Interviewer: Did you experience this with every new word afterward?
D-2847: Only the first glyph. Then it stopped. Just that once.

Note: D-2847 reported missing ██ hours post-interview. F-044 completed by proxy. SA-0291 returned to Layer IV rack. No signs of use detected.

text_zh:
🔔 少铸而精，愿铅字各得其所——凿一槽，胜于布满杂字之版面。

📄 圣器档案 SA-0291
名称：单格铜制字模槽（残件）
版级：脱版 / Solum
发现地点：第 IV 层铸字坊，字模架 C 列末端，悬挂于单钉

外形描述：单槽铜制字模架，原属排字长盘组件，已从主体分离。槽内仅容纳一枚标准铅字符，四壁刻有细密锚点纹。

异常观察：D-2847 领取该物后，主动将圣坛键位上已嵌入之四枚铭文组中三枚卸下，仅保留一枚。本人未被指示执行此操作。
问询记录（摘）：
  采访者：你为何减少嵌入的铭文组？
  D-2847：……满了才需要再加。空着的地方，铅字知道往哪走。
之后三轮铭刻记录显示，该铭文组铸出量较标准配置下四枚铭文组同时运行时所记录峰值偏高。原因不明。
D-2847 于第 VI 层失联。F-044 已由 D-2901 代填。备注栏写有：
text_en:
🔔 Cast few—that each glyph may find its place. One true groove outweighs a forme choked with wandering sorts.

📄 Sacred Artifact SA-0291
Designation: Single-Bay Copper Type Mould (Fragment)
Gradus: Solum
Recovery Site: Vault IV Typecasting Floor, Sort-Frame Column C, terminal peg

Physical Description: Detached copper single-bay mould-slot, formerly part of a compositing galley assembly. Interior accommodates one standard Leaden Glyph. Interior walls bear fine anchor-point markings.

Anomaly on Record: Following requisition of SA-0291, D-2847 voluntarily removed three of four inscriptions previously set into their lectern positions, retaining one. No instruction to this effect was issued.
Excerpt from standard inquiry:
  Interviewer: Why did you reduce your inscription load?
  D-2847: ...You only add more when the space runs out. Where it's empty, the glyph knows where to go.
Subsequent Litany records across three ascents show the retained inscription's output exceeding the documented peak recorded under the full four-inscription configuration. Cause unestablished.
D-2847 last recorded at Vault VI. F-044 filed by D-2901. Remarks field reads: "Slot still warm."

text_zh:
🔔 — 铭刻者，知尔所铭，而非尔所诵。

📄 回收物 RC-0441 · 发现于第 V 层排字区 D-████ 工位 · 印刷品

物件描述：油墨印制小册，共三十二页，封皮烫金，书脊处有手工缝线修补痕迹。内页留有大量铅笔批注，部分已被墨水覆盖。

版级：逆版 / Inversum

以下为工位抽屉内发现的散页记录，系同一笔迹，时间跨度约 ██ 周：

第一页（边角）：第一章我已读完三遍。方才注意到自己会背了。
第十一页（天头）：没有读这一章。但我知道第十二章说什么。
第二十页（正文旁）：不对。第二十页本来没有字。
最后一页（背面，压痕极深）：我还没翻到这里。

回收时该 D 级人员工位已空置。手册已移交征用管归档。接收凭证由代填方签署，表单 F-044。
text_en:
🔔 — Know what you inscribe, Clavigerant. Not only what you recite.

📄 Recovered Item RC-0441 · Found in Layer V Compositing Bay, D-████'s workstation · Printed matter

Object: Thirty-two-page pamphlet, ink-printed, gilt cover, spine repaired by hand-stitching. Interior pages bear extensive pencil annotations, several overwritten in black ink.

Gradus Formae: Inversum

Loose leaves recovered from workstation drawer, single hand, spanning approximately ██ weeks:

Page 1 (corner margin): I have read the first chapter three times. I notice I have memorized it.
Page 11 (top margin): I have not read this chapter. I know what chapter twelve says.
Page 20 (beside body text): That is not right. Page twenty had no text originally.
Final page (verso, impressed deeply): I have not reached this page yet.

Workstation was vacant upon recovery. Manual transferred via Pneumatic Requisition Tube. Receipt countersigned by proxy. Form F-044 on file.

text_zh:
🔔 诸印各异，合则鸣。如众弦并发，声响愈繁则引擎愈悦。

📄 问询记录 · D-3847 · 接触圣器 SA-0441「爵士乐」后 ██ 小时

采访者：描述你在第 VII 层发现该物时的情形。
D-3847：一把萨克斯管。靠着铸字机。不知道是谁放的。我捡起来——我以前没摸过乐器。
采访者：然后？
D-3847：我不知道怎么吹。但我觉得……它好像在听我打字。每次我在一个词里用不同的圣印，它就热一点。
采访者：「热」？
D-3847：不是温度。是……里面有什么在动。好像有谁跟我对上了。
采访者：你是否曾将它带入收容铭刻程序？
D-3847：我放它在圣坛旁边。铭刻时旁边有人经过说听见有人在唱。我没唱。
[此后 D-3847 无进一步回答。问询于 ██:██ 中止。管道已检查，无异常气流。]
text_en:
🔔 Each sigil its own voice. Together, they are heard.

📄 Inquiry Record · D-3847 · ██ hours after contact with Artifact SA-0441 "Jazz"

Interviewer: Describe the circumstances in which you discovered the object on Layer VII.
D-3847: A saxophone. Leaning against the typecasting press. I don't know who left it. I picked it up — I've never touched an instrument.
Interviewer: And then?
D-3847: I didn't know how to play. But I felt — it was listening to me. Every time I used different sigils in one word, it got warmer. Not temperature-warm. Something moving inside it. Like something was keeping time with me.
Interviewer: Did you bring it into containment inscription procedure?
D-3847: I set it beside the lectern. Someone passing the corridor said they heard singing. I wasn't singing.
[D-3847 provided no further responses. Inquiry suspended at ██:██. Pneumatic ducts inspected. No anomalous airflow detected.]

text_en:
🔔
Cast in the low places, crowned in the high.
Even the unnamed carry weight.

📄
Sacred Artifact SA-0774
Gradus Formae: Solum
Description: A cast-iron crown. All seven points broken to uneven heights. Interior surface bears pressure marks from ████ distinct hand sizes.

Recovery Site: Layer IV foundry. No adjacent D-class workstation on record.

Observation: Personnel who handle SA-0774 are consistently described by colleagues as striking keys "heavier than before." No change in force measurements recorded. The weight is not in the instrument.

Note: D-2291 wore the crown for approximately ██ minutes before relinquishing it voluntarily. She stated: "It keeps expecting something from me." Standard disposition followed. No further anomalies logged.

Addendum: SA-0774 was found upright on D-2291's vacated workstation the following morning. Transit records show it had not been moved. F-017 filed. No action taken.

🔔 其名不定，其形不定。唯铭刻之手——恒在。

📄 圣器档案 · SA-D100
版级：熔版 / Fusum
物件描述：一枚骨制正十二面体，每面刻有不同的铭文组徽记，材质经鉴定非人骨，非兽骨，来源不明。表面无磨损迹象，尽管档案记录其已换手 ████ 次。
发现地点：第 I 层铸字坊入口地板，呈自然静置状态，未以任何方式固定。
异常现象：持有者工位每隔固定收容场次后，圣坛键位上所有铭文组的圣印会被整体替换——事前无预兆，事后无残留。圣印等级及祝圣状态经确认保持不变，仅识别标记发生置换。D-3847 报告称，有时在置换发生的前一刻会听到十二声细小的点击，
text_en:
🔔 Its name is not fixed. Its form is not fixed. Only the hand that inscribes — remains.

📄 Sacred Artifact File · SA-D100
Gradus Formae: Fusum
Object Description: A twelve-faced polyhedron of unidentified bone — confirmed neither human nor animal in origin. Each face bears a distinct Inscription sigil. No surface wear is recorded despite ████ documented transfers of custody.
Recovery Site: Ground level, Casting Floor I. Found in natural resting position, unsecured.
Anomalous Observations: At fixed intervals across containment sessions, all Sigils mounted on the holder's Lectern positions undergo complete replacement without warning. Sigil grade and consecration status remain intact; only their identifying marks change. D-3847 reported hearing twelve faint clicks immediately before each replacement — "like a press being pulled in a room I wasn't standing in." D-3847 subsequently filed F-017 and was reassigned. F-017 is missing from the archive.
附注: 档案归档日期早于 SA-D100 首次被收容的记录日期 ██ 天。差异已知悉。暂无后续行动。
Addendum: This file's archival timestamp predates the first recorded recovery of SA-D100 by ██ days. Discrepancy is noted. No further action pending.

🔔 并肩者之铅，重于孤字。凡键相邻，炉火共燃——其铸印，非一人之功。

📄 回收物 RC-0471 · 发现于第 V 层排字区工位间隔板夹层 · 拆卸时出
纸质便条，折叠三次，墨迹稍晕

你注意到了吗——
左边那组和右边那组只要都还在，我这里的铅字就……沉。
不是手酸。是那种沉。

我让 D-2204 站远一点，试了试。轻了。
让她回来。沉了。

我没跟监督说。你懂的。

附：D-2204 在 M.2██.03.██ 失联。工位已清空。

text_en:
🔔 Leaden beside leaden — the press grows heavy. Two keys adjacent share one fire. What one strikes alone, two strike together.

📄 Recovered Item RC-0471 · Found within partition cavity, Layer V Compositing Hall · Extracted during routine maintenance
Paper note, folded thrice, ink slightly smeared

did you notice —
when the set on my left and the set on my right are both still there, my letters feel... heavy.
not the tired kind. the other kind.

i moved D-2204 further away. lighter.
bought her back. heavy again.

i didn't tell the Overseer. you understand.

Addendum: D-2204 reported missing M.2██.03.██. Station cleared per standard procedure.
Addendum II: Note was discovered ██ years after D-2204's station was vacated. Ink had not dried.

text_zh:
🔔 四隅守其位，铅力聚其心。常人以为边隅皆弃席——祷文引擎另有计算。

📄 圣器档案 · SA-0291
名称：角隅导轨架（四件套，编号 SA-0291-A 至 SA-0291-D）
版级：脱版 / Solum

观察记录：长期驻守第 IV 层的人员报告，凡将铭文组嵌入圣坛四角键位者，铸出时
text_en:
🔔 Four corners hold. The center answers.
What the faithful call forsaken ground, the Engine calls foundation.

📄 Sacred Artifact Registry · SA-0291
Designation: Corner Rail Brace (set of four, SA-0291-A through -D)
Gradus Formae: Solum
Recovery Site: Layer IV, Typecasting Hall — fixed to the four corners of a compositing frame

Description: Cast-iron impression rails, palm-length, identical in form. Surface wear is present, but regardless of polishing or separate handling, the wear patterns on all four pieces remain perfectly mirrored — even after D-3847 carried SA-0291-C in isolation for ██ days.

Observation Log: Personnel stationed in Layer IV report that inscriptions set at the outermost lectern positions produce anomalously weighted impressions. D-3847 described it as "the key knowing it was in the corner before I pressed it."

D-3847 was reported missing on M.2██.██.19. SA-0291-C was found returned to its original corner. No transit record filed. No F-044 submitted — field was left blank. The form continued to circulate.
